slides.prompt: Template Metaprogramming (TMP) is a technique where the compiler executes code at compile time using template instantiation recursion, computing constants or generating types before runtime execution.

slides.title: Recursion Termination in TMP
slides.prompt: How is compile-time loop recursion terminated in traditional TMP struct calculators?
options: Through template specialization serving as the base case
By using standard break or return statements
slides.correctAnswer: Through template specialization serving as the base case

slides.title: Turing Completeness of C++ Templates
slides.prompt: What does it mean that C++ template instantiation is Turing complete?
options: Any computable algorithm can theoretically be calculated at compile time using template metaprogramming
Templates can run embedded assembly code at runtime
Template code automatically optimizes runtime CPU threads
Templates can bypass host operating system security restrictions
slides.correctAnswer: Any computable algorithm can theoretically be calculated at compile time using template metaprogramming

slides.title: Drawback of Excessive TMP Recursion
slides.prompt: What risk is associated with deep template recursion in classic TMP?
options: Exceeding compiler template instantiation depth limits and causing long build times
Stack overflow exceptions during runtime execution
Dynamic memory leakage on the heap
slides.correctAnswer: Exceeding compiler template instantiation depth limits and causing long build times

slides.title: TMP vs constexpr Functions
slides.prompt: Why are modern C++ standards shifting towards constexpr/consteval functions over classic struct-based TMP?
options: constexpr functions offer cleaner, imperative syntax that is easier to read and debug
Classic TMP cannot compute mathematical expressions
constexpr functions run strictly faster at runtime than TMP
slides.correctAnswer: constexpr functions offer cleaner, imperative syntax that is easier to read and debug
